name: GitHub MCP Server
use_when: the agent needs to read and act on GitHub issues, pull requests, code and Actions
install: remote https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/ or local Docker image with GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN

name: Playwright MCP
use_when: the agent needs to open, click through and check a real browser page through the accessibility tree

name: Chrome DevTools MCP
use_when: you want the agent to read console, network and performance traces from Chrome while debugging

name: shadcn MCP server
use_when: you want the agent to browse, search and install components from shadcn and other registries set in components.json

name: Supabase MCP Server
use_when: the agent needs to manage tables, read config and query data in a Supabase project

name: Sentry MCP
use_when: the agent should read production errors and issues from Sentry while fixing bugs
note: npm package metadata points to getsentry/toolkit; GitHub page is getsentry/sentry-mcp

name: Next.js DevTools MCP
use_when: you build with Next.js and want the agent to read the dev server's errors and Next.js docs

name: Figma MCP server
license: Figma Developer Terms (not open source); free Starter use limited to 6 tool calls a month
install: claude mcp add --transport http figma https://mcp.figma.com/mcp
note: Full use needs a Dev or Full seat on a paid plan. Free option: export design tokens and screenshots by hand.

name: Agent Skills specification
use_when: you write a SKILL.md and need the exact format rules, best practices and the list of clients that load skills

name: skills-ref
use_when: you want to check a skill folder against the spec before publishing it
install: from the skills-ref/ folder of agentskills/agentskills
note: an npm package named skills-ref (MIT) exists but its metadata has no repository link; not confirmed to be the same tool

name: Context7
license: MIT (MCP server); the API backend and crawler are closed
use_when: the agent needs current, version-specific docs and code examples for a library instead of its training data
install: npx ctx7 setup, or remote https://mcp.context7.com/mcp (API key recommended for higher limits)

name: Blender MCP
use_when: you want an agent to drive a running Blender over MCP to build or edit scenes
install: claude mcp add blender uvx mcp-for-blender, then uvx mcp-for-blender install-addon
note: PyPI package is mcp-for-blender; needs Blender installed and the add-on enabled

name: Blockbench
use_when: you want low-poly or blocky models with pixel-art textures, quick to learn
install: download, or use the web app

name: FreeCAD
use_when: you need precise parametric CAD parts rather than artistic models

name: SVGO
use_when: you want to shrink and clean SVG files from the command line or a build step

name: Krita
use_when: you need to paint illustrations, textures or concept art with a tablet
note: GitHub repo is a mirror of invent.kde.org/graphics/krita

name: Pixelorama
use_when: you want a free open-source pixel art and sprite animation editor

name: Aseprite
license: paid; source available under the Aseprite EULA (some modules MIT)

name: rembg
use_when: you need to remove image backgrounds locally from a script or CLI

name: Squoosh
use_when: you want to compress and convert images (WebP, AVIF) and compare quality side by side
install: web app; the npm CLI @squoosh/cli exists but its status was not checked

name: Penpot
use_when: you want an open-source Figma-style design and prototyping tool you can self-host
install: web app, or self-host with Docker (https://penpot.app/self-host)

name: Excalidraw
use_when: you want quick hand-drawn style diagrams and wireframes
install: web app, or npm i @excalidraw/excalidraw to embed

name: tldraw
license: custom tldraw license (npm says SEE LICENSE IN LICENSE.md)
use_when: you want to embed a whiteboard canvas in your own app
note: reported to need a license key in production; license file not read

name: Figma
license: free plan for individuals (3 projects, 2 members, 30-day version history); paid plans beyond that

name: Burst
license: Burst license, mostly "Shopify some rights reserved" (some photos CC0)
use_when: you need product, e-commerce and small-business photos
note: Check each photo's license; CC0 photos are listed at https://burst.shopify.com/licenses/creative-commons

name: StockSnap
use_when: you want photos that are CC0 so they can sit in a repo without license questions

name: Openverse
license: per item (CC licenses and public domain); the code is MIT
use_when: you want one search (and API) across many openly licensed image and audio sources, filterable by license
install: openverse.org search, or its public API
note: Each result keeps its own CC license; read it and credit where required. Catalog docs https://make.wordpress.org/openverse/handbook/openverse-catalog/

name: Wikimedia Commons
license: per file (public domain, CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA and others)
use_when: you need a photo or diagram of a real place, thing or historic subject
note: Read each file's license; CC BY-SA needs credit and share-alike. Not all files are free of trademark or personality rights.

name: NASA Image and Video Library
license: generally not copyrighted (US government work); see NASA media guidelines
use_when: you need space, Earth and spaceflight images, video or audio
note: NASA logos and insignia are restricted (https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/nasa-logo-use/); don't imply NASA endorsement; some items are third-party.

name: Library of Congress Free to Use and Reuse
license: public domain or no known restrictions (per set)
use_when: you want themed sets of historic American photos, posters and maps that are cleared for reuse

name: Rijksmuseum
license: public domain images (CC0) for most collection items; see data policy
use_when: you want Dutch Golden Age paintings and prints in high resolution
install: download from the collection, or the data services

name: The Public Domain Review
license: curated public-domain works; rights label on each item
note: A curated guide that links to the source archives; see https://publicdomainreview.org/reusing-material/

name: Open Peeps
use_when: you want hand-drawn people you can mix and match and keep in a repo

name: Humaaans
use_when: you want flat, colourful people illustrations you can recombine

name: Open Doodles
use_when: you want loose, sketchy people illustrations with no credit needed

name: unDraw
use_when: you want flat scene illustrations recolourable to your brand colour
install: download by hand from undraw.co (link only; no scripted fetching)
note: No credit needed. Bans automated scraping/downloading, redistribution in packs, competing services and AI training.

name: Blush
use_when: you want customizable illustrations from many artists in one editor
note: Commercial use allowed, credit not required; no compiling to build a competing service.

name: Storyset
use_when: you want editable, animatable scene illustrations and can show a credit
note: Credit required on free use (or a Flaticon Premium plan); no redistribution, resale or stock/archive use.

name: DrawKit
use_when: you want polished illustration packs for landing pages and apps
note: Credit not required; no standalone redistribution, no templates or merch, no AI training.

name: IRA Design
use_when: you want to build simple gradient or outline illustrations from components
note: Older project; no recent update date shown.

name: Kenney
use_when: you want consistent low-poly 3D, 2D and UI game assets you can ship anywhere

name: Poly Haven Models
use_when: you want realistic, scanned-quality props for a three.js or Blender scene
install: download glTF/Blend/FBX, or the Poly Haven API

name: Sketchfab
license: per model (CC licenses for free downloads; paid store licenses)
use_when: you need a specific object and can check each model's license
install: download, or the Sketchfab Download API
note: Filter by downloadable + license; respect NoAI tags and CC BY credit; store models are paid.

name: Poly Haven
use_when: you need HDRI lighting or PBR textures for a 3D scene
install: download, or the Poly Haven API
note: Assets may be redistributed; the site itself bans scraping without permission, so use the API.

name: ambientCG
use_when: you want a large set of PBR materials and HDRIs, with an API

name: ShareTextures
use_when: you want more CC0 PBR textures, especially architectural surfaces

name: Three.js
use_when: you need a general WebGL/WebGPU 3D library with the largest ecosystem

name: Babylon.js
use_when: you want a full engine with built-in physics, GUI, inspector and an online playground

name: PlayCanvas Engine
use_when: you are building a browser game or configurator and want an engine with an optional hosted editor
note: The engine is MIT; the hosted editor has free and paid plans.

name: A-Frame
use_when: you want VR/AR scenes written as HTML tags on top of three.js
install: npm i aframe (or a script tag)

name: model-viewer
use_when: you only need to show one glTF model with orbit controls and AR, no custom scene code

name: postprocessing
use_when: you need bloom, depth of field or other post effects in plain three.js with merged passes

name: React Three Fiber
use_when: you build three.js scenes inside a React app

name: drei
use_when: you want ready helpers for R3F: controls, loaders, environment maps, text, staging

name: react-postprocessing
use_when: you want post effects (bloom, vignette, SSAO) as R3F components

name: react-three-rapier
use_when: you need rigid-body physics in a React Three Fiber scene

name: JoltPhysics.js
use_when: you need heavier physics (many bodies, vehicles, characters) from the Jolt engine compiled to WASM

name: glTF Transform
use_when: you need to shrink and clean glTF/GLB files (Draco or Meshopt, texture resize, KTX2/WebP)

name: Draco
use_when: you want the smallest mesh geometry and accept slower decoding
install: npm i draco3d (decoders also ship with three.js)

name: meshoptimizer / gltfpack
use_when: you want fast-decoding mesh and animation compression (EXT_meshopt_compression)
install: npm i meshoptimizer; gltfpack from the releases page

name: gltf.report
license: free web app, not open source
use_when: you want to inspect a model's size, meshes and textures and run glTF Transform scripts in the browser

name: gltf-pipeline
use_when: you want a simple CLI to convert glTF to GLB and apply Draco

name: Spline
license: freemium; paid plans remove the web export watermark
note: Free option: Blender plus glTF Transform, loaded with three.js or R3F.

name: three.js examples
use_when: you want working code for a three.js feature (loaders, materials, post effects, WebGPU)
install: open in browser; source is in the three.js repo under examples/

name: three.js manual
use_when: you want step-by-step explanations of three.js basics and common tasks

name: R3F scaling performance
use_when: your R3F scene is slow and you need the official advice (on-demand rendering, instancing, LOD)

name: Discover three.js
license: free to read, not open source
use_when: you want a free book that teaches three.js app structure from the start

name: pmndrs examples
use_when: you want many small R3F demos with source to copy patterns from
install: open in browser; clone the repo for source

name: three-mesh-bvh
use_when: raycasting or collision against large meshes is slow

name: Three.js Journey
note: Free option: Discover three.js and the three.js manual.

name: Recharts
use_when: you need standard line, bar, area and pie charts in a React app

name: Chart.js
use_when: you want simple canvas charts without a framework, or in plain HTML

use_when: you need many chart types, large datasets, or dashboards with zoom and brushing

name: D3

name: Nivo

name: Plotly.js

name: React Router (framework mode, formerly Remix)
use_when: you want a React full-stack app built on web standards (loaders, actions, forms) without Next.js
note: Remix v2 merged into React Router v7; React Router v8 is out.

name: SvelteKit
use_when: you prefer Svelte over React and want routing, SSR and adapters in one package

name: Nuxt
use_when: the project uses Vue and needs SSR, file routing and modules

name: TanStack Start
use_when: you want type-safe routing from TanStack Router plus server functions, on Vite

name: Qwik
use_when: you need very little JavaScript sent on first load (resumability instead of hydration)

name: Angular
use_when: the team wants a full, opinionated framework with DI, forms and router built in

name: Starlight
use_when: you are building a documentation site and want Astro underneath

name: VitePress
use_when: you want a fast Markdown docs site with Vue components

name: Docusaurus
use_when: you want a React docs site with versioning, i18n and a blog built in

name: Eleventy (Build Awesome)
use_when: you want a plain, template-based static site with no client framework
note: Eleventy is being renamed Build Awesome (v4); npm still lists @11ty/eleventy, repo field points to 11ty/buildawesome (11ty/eleventy redirects).

name: Hugo
use_when: you want a single binary that builds large Markdown sites very fast, no Node needed
install: prebuilt binary or package manager (brew install hugo); not on npm

name: Rspack
use_when: you are moving off webpack and want its config and loaders with a faster Rust core

name: esbuild
use_when: you need a small, very fast bundler or transpiler for libraries, scripts or CLIs

name: Bun
use_when: you want one tool for runtime, package manager, bundler and test runner
install: curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash (or npm i -g bun)
note: the npm package installs the Bun binary; the main install is the shell script.

name: Turbopack
use_when: you are on Next.js; it is the Next.js bundler and is not used on its own
install: built into next (next dev / next build); no separate package
note: repo is shared with Next.js, so its stars and activity are Next.js's.

use_when: you want type-safe styles written in TypeScript that compile to static CSS

use_when: you want CSS-in-JS syntax and design tokens with no runtime cost

use_when: you want a Tailwind-like utility setup that is fully configurable through presets

name: Open Props
use_when: you want ready design tokens as CSS variables on top of plain CSS

name: Zustand
use_when: you need a small global client-state store with hooks and little boilerplate

name: Jotai
use_when: you want state split into small atoms that components subscribe to one by one

name: SWR
use_when: you want a lighter fetch-and-cache hook than TanStack Query

name: Redux Toolkit
use_when: the app is large, already uses Redux, or needs strict, traceable state changes

name: tRPC
use_when: client and server are both TypeScript and you want typed API calls without a schema file

use_when: you need a schema for validation and TypeScript types from one source (pairs with any form library)

name: Valibot
use_when: you want Zod-style schemas with a smaller bundle through tree-shaking

name: FastMCP

name: MCP Inspector

use_when: you need to test and debug an MCP server in a browser, CLI or terminal UI

name: MCP reference servers
license: see LICENSE in repo (npm says "SEE LICENSE IN LICENSE")
use_when: you want working example servers to copy patterns from or run as-is

name: Typst

install: cargo install --locked typst-cli, brew install typst, or download a release binary; typst compile doc.typ

name: WeasyPrint
use_when: you already have HTML and CSS and want print-quality PDFs from Python without a browser

name: React-PDF
use_when: you build PDFs from React components in the browser or on Node, with its own flexbox layout

name: Playwright page.pdf()
use_when: you want a PDF of a real web page exactly as headless Chromium prints it

name: Pandoc
use_when: you convert Markdown, DOCX or HTML into PDF, DOCX, EPUB and other formats
install: see https://pandoc.org/installing.html (apt install pandoc, brew install pandoc); needs a PDF engine such as Typst, WeasyPrint or LaTeX

name: Puppeteer
use_when: you are already on Puppeteer and want headless Chrome to print pages to PDF

name: pdfme
use_when: you want a drag-and-drop template designer plus JSON data to generate forms, invoices and labels
install: npm i @pdfme/generator @pdfme/common (add @pdfme/ui for the WYSIWYG designer)

name: TeX Live
license: free software, mixed licenses (LPPL, GPL and others per package)
use_when: you need the complete LaTeX distribution with every package and engine (pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX, LuaLaTeX)

name: Gotenberg
use_when: you want an HTTP service that turns HTML, URLs, Markdown and Office files into PDF (Chromium and LibreOffice inside)

name: Vivliostyle CLI
use_when: you typeset books from Markdown or HTML with CSS Paged Media, including vertical Japanese text
note: AGPL; fine as a build tool, check terms before bundling into a served product.

name: Prince
license: paid; free non-commercial license adds a logo to page one
note: Strongest CSS Paged Media support. Free option: WeasyPrint or Vivliostyle.

name: qpdf
use_when: you need to merge, split, rotate, decrypt, linearize or repair PDFs from the command line without changing content
install: apt install qpdf or brew install qpdf

name: pikepdf
use_when: you want qpdf's robustness from Python, including low-level object edits and repairing damaged files

name: PyMuPDF
use_when: you need fast rendering, text extraction, redaction and page edits in one Python library and can accept AGPL
note: AGPL; a closed-source product or service needs the paid Artifex license. Same engine as MuPDF / mutool.

name: PDFtk Server (pdftk-java)
license: GPL-2.0-or-later; redistribution in non-GPL commercial products needs a paid license
use_when: you want the classic one-line commands for merging, splitting, stamping and filling forms
install: apt install pdftk-java or brew install pdftk-java
note: The original C++ PDFtk is unmaintained; pdftk-java is the maintained port that distros ship.

name: Stirling-PDF
license: MIT core; Pro and Enterprise features under a proprietary license
use_when: you want a self-hosted web app and API with dozens of PDF operations (merge, convert, OCR, sign)
note: Some features are not open source; check which build you run.

name: Docling
use_when: you turn PDFs, DOCX, PPTX and images into Markdown or JSON with layout, tables and reading order, for LLM use

name: pdfplumber
use_when: you need exact text positions, lines and tables from digital (not scanned) PDFs

name: PDF.js
use_when: you render or read text from PDFs in the browser or Node with JavaScript

name: Marker
license: Apache-2.0 code; model weights under modified AI Pubs Open Rail-M (free for research, personal use and startups under $5M)
use_when: you want PDFs (including equations and tables) converted to Markdown with deep-learning layout models
note: Larger companies need a paid license for the weights.

name: Unstructured
use_when: you split many file types into typed elements (titles, tables, text) for RAG pipelines

name: Apache Tika
use_when: you need text and metadata out of more than a thousand file types through one Java server
install: run the tika-server jar or Docker image; Python client via pip install tika

name: MinerU
license: MinerU Open Source License (custom; read before commercial use)
use_when: you convert complex PDFs (papers, formulas, Chinese text) to Markdown or JSON

name: unpdf
use_when: you extract text or images from PDFs in serverless or edge JavaScript runtimes (PDF.js build without the DOM)

name: Camelot
use_when: you only need tables out of digital PDFs, straight into pandas DataFrames

name: OCRmyPDF
use_when: you add a searchable text layer to scanned PDFs in one command, with PDF/A output
install: pip install ocrmypdf (needs Tesseract and Ghostscript), or apt install ocrmypdf

name: Tesseract
use_when: you need the standard open OCR engine for images, with 100+ languages

name: PaddleOCR
use_when: you need higher accuracy on hard scans, photos, Chinese and mixed layouts than Tesseract gives

name: docTR
use_when: you want a deep-learning OCR pipeline (detection plus recognition) on PyTorch

name: Tesseract.js
use_when: you need OCR in the browser or Node without a native install

name: pytesseract
use_when: you call Tesseract from Python on images you already have in memory

name: LaTeXTemplates.com
license: per template (mostly LPPL, MIT, CC BY); some have no license
use_when: you want curated, well-kept LaTeX templates for books, theses, CVs and reports
install: download the .zip from each template page
note: Treat templates with no listed license as all rights reserved.

name: Overleaf template gallery
license: per template (Overleaf recommends LPPL for templates)
use_when: you need a journal, conference or university template, often the official one
install: open in Overleaf or download the source zip

name: pdfme templates
use_when: you want starting JSON templates (invoices, certificates, labels) for pdfme
install: copy a template JSON from the pdfme playground; use with @pdfme/generator

name: Scribus
use_when: you need page layout with CMYK, spot colors and PDF/X export for a print shop
install: apt install scribus, or download from scribus.net; scriptable with Python

name: MDN @page reference
use_when: you need page size, margins and page selectors for print CSS

name: CSS Paged Media Module Level 3 (W3C)

name: Scribus color management guide
